nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on the same vertex set. Then $H$ equals the square of $G$ if and only if, for all vertices $u$ and $v$, the vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $H$ exactly when $u \ne v$ and either $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ or there is a vertex $w$ with $u$ adjacent to $w$ and $w$ adjacent to $v$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the graph square

nodes.summary: In a 2-vertex-connected simple graph on a finite vertex set with at least five vertices, every vertex has at least four neighbors in the square of the graph.
nodes.title: Minimum degree in the square of a 2-connected graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $u, w, v, x_1, \dots, x_k$ (with $k \ge 0$) be a sequence of vertices in which consecutive vertices are adjacent in $G$. If $u \ne v$, then in the sequence $u, v, x_1, \dots, x_k$ consecutive vertices are adjacent in the square of $G$.
nodes.title: Skipping a vertex of a walk in the graph square

nodes.summary: If a simple graph $G$ is connected, then the square of $G$ is connected.
nodes.title: The square of a connected graph is connected

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ and vertices $u$ and $v$, the vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in the square of $G$ if and only if $u \ne v$ and either $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ or there is a vertex $w$ with $u$ adjacent to $w$ and $w$ adjacent to $v$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the graph square

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on the same finite vertex set such that every edge of $G$ is an edge of $H$. If the square of $G$ is Hamiltonian, then the square of $H$ is Hamiltonian.
nodes.title: Adding edges preserves a Hamiltonian square

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on the same vertex set such that every edge of $G$ is an edge of $H$. Then every edge of the square of $G$ is an edge of the square of $H$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the graph square

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_n$ be vertices with $n \ge 3$ and $v_0 = v_n$, such that $v_1, \dots, v_n$ are pairwise distinct and every vertex of $V$ is among them. If for each $i < n$ the vertices $v_i$ and $v_{i+1}$ are distinct and either adjacent in $G$ or have a common neighbor in $G$, then the square of $G$ is Hamiltonian.
nodes.title: A cyclic listing by square adjacencies gives a Hamiltonian square

nodes.summary: The square of a simple graph $G$ is the simple graph on the same vertex set in which two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when they are adjacent in $G$ or have a common neighbor in $G$, that is, a vertex $w$ adjacent in $G$ to both $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Square of a graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
